personas.name: Maya

seat_height_in.rationale: ADA transfer range; lower = hard to push up from, higher = hard to slide onto laterally

personas.name: Carlos

seat_height_in.rationale: Below 19 strains lumbar on standing; above 22 dangles feet and shifts pelvis

personas.context_for_agent: L4-L5 fusion 18 months ago. Cleared for daily activity but soft cushions flare his back within ten minutes. Works from a sit-stand desk; the sofa is the evening rest space.

personas.name: Eleanor

seat_height_in.rationale: Below 18 strains knees on standing; above 20 dangles feet

personas.context_for_agent: Lives independently. Reads three hours a day. Last upholstered chair sank too soft and she struggled to stand without help. Wants to keep her independence.

personas.name: Sam
personas.transfer_strategy: fits a frame standard sofas weren't dimensioned for

seat_height_in.rationale: Below 19 puts his knees above his hips (uncomfortable, wrecks the back); above 22 lifts heels off the floor

personas.context_for_agent: Software engineer. Three sofas in four years; all felt like child furniture and went back. His wife is done. Needs deeper-than-standard depth, a back that actually reaches his shoulder blades, and a verified weight rating he doesn't have to hope about.

personas.name: Priya
personas.transfer_strategy: gentle stand-up without engaging the abdominal incision

seat_height_in.rationale: Below 18 forces ab engagement to stand; above 20 makes feeding posture awkward

constraints.delivery_preference: white-glove (cannot move heavy with incision restrictions)

personas.context_for_agent: First-time parent. Living room is recovery space and feeding space. Current sectional is too soft to push up from and too deep to hold the baby on a propped pillow. Needs firmness, shallow depth, armrest leverage, and material that survives spit-up.
